_comment: WHAT THE STUDY RUNS. One file, because the scheme is implemented twice and the
two implementations have already drifted apart once without anything noticing
This file is READ BY TESTS ON BOTH SIDES, not just documented. rust/tests/
noise_gates.rs parses it and asserts the injector's own condition list and CLI
defaults agree with it; scripts/test_noise_conditions.py asserts every name here
resolves in noiseInject.CONDITIONS to the same parameters. A previous settings
file, scripts/noise_strategy_params.json, was never passed to the binary at all
and so silently meant nothing for the life of the project. This one fails a test
The names are the condition keys shared by both injectors.
Settled 2026-08-27 by the author, on the evidence in RERUN_PLAN.md section 13.9
and NOISE_DESIGN.md section 5.8: twelve replicates on real QM9, every condition
delivering the same amount of noise. Shape and contamination do not earn

stage_1_full_grid.name: gaussian
stage_1_full_grid.why: The reference case, and what both direct predecessors used, so the results stay comparable to theirs.

stage_1_full_grid.name: grouped_wider
stage_1_full_grid.why: Whole scaffold families get a larger error, still centred on the truth. Indistinguishable from Gaussian on its own -- it is here because it is the comparator that makes grouped_shifted interpretable. The pair is the claim; neither half is.

stage_1_full_grid.name: grouped_shifted
stage_1_full_grid.why: Whole scaffold families pushed in one direction. The ONLY zero-mean condition that separates: against grouped_wider at level 1.5 it costs 0.0963 R2 on the random forest and 0.1419 on LightGBM, at 2.52x and 2.71x the run-to-run spread, paired t p = 0.0031 and 0.0002. The wider range quoted before 2026-08-27 (0.096 to 0.314 at up to 7.4x) included a Ridge row, and Ridge is not in the study. Same amount of noise, same families, same targeting -- the only difference is direction.

stage_1_full_grid.name: censoring
stage_1_full_grid.why: Values past the assay limit recorded as the limit. The most prevalent real mechanism, not zero-mean, and it cannot be dose-matched, so it runs on its own axis (fraction of labels clipped).

qm9_scope.why: The author's call: on QM9 censoring runs on about five model-and-representation pairs, not all 78, because the question there is how big the effect is and not which model resists it best. 350 runs instead of 5460. Which five comes from the screen, like the deep run's selection (RERUN_PLAN.md 13.13). This scope is QM9 ONLY -- censoring stays a full condition in the uncertainty runs on the experimental datasets, where it is one of only two conditions that can answer the which-molecules question.
qm9_scope.paper_must_say: Censoring was run on a named subset of pairs to measure the size of its effect, not to compare models or representations under it. No claim about WHICH model resists censoring best can rest on this run.

stage_2_depth_only.name: student_t_nu5
stage_2_depth_only.why: One tail weight, not three. The three settings are within 0.0036 R2 of each other and of Gaussian at the reporting level, against a test that could have seen 0.0076 to 0.0120 -- that being what the model carrying each effect could itself have detected, not the best model's threshold quoted against another model's effect, which is what this file said before 2026-08-27. Every figure here is on the two roster models at twelve replicates; the wider ranges quoted before 2026-08-27 were Ridge rows, and Ridge is not in the study. nu = 10 is nearly Gaussian by construction; nu = 3's per-run delivered dose has a 17% spread at level 1.5, which makes it the worst-behaved thing on the grid to report. nu = 5 is mid-ladder and well-behaved.

stage_2_depth_only.name: outlier_p10
stage_2_depth_only.why: One contamination fraction, not three. Same evidence: the largest step of the 1% -> 5% -> 10% ladder is 0.0049 R2 and the largest of the three against Gaussian is 0.0047. p = 10% is the top of Hampel's published range and the strongest contamination, so if anything is ever going to show, it shows there.

stage_2_depth_only.name: laplace
stage_2_depth_only.why: Kept, settled by the author 2026-08-27. Empirically indistinguishable from Gaussian on every roster model at both levels tested. The largest difference anywhere is 0.0136 R2 -- LightGBM at level 1.5, against a replicate-to-replicate spread of 0.0574, so 0.24 of the wobble, paired t p = 0.350. At the reporting level it is 0.0024. Two earlier figures here, 0.0058 and 0.0087, were both wrong: the first was a Ridge row and Ridge is not in the study, the second understated the level-1.5 difference. Corrected 2026-08-27 from results/setting_selection_test.csv, so it buys a citation rather than a result -- but it is the only distribution family actually FITTED to real bioactivity error, and at 720 training runs (1.4% of the old design) the citation is cheap. Depth stage only; it is not in the full grid.

not_run.name: student_t_nu10
not_run.why: Within 0.0017 R2 of Gaussian at the reporting level (0.10 of the run-to-run spread, paired t p = 0.698), and within 0.0019 of nu = 5. Represented by student_t_nu5.

not_run.name: student_t_nu3
not_run.why: Within 0.0036 R2 of Gaussian at the reporting level (0.22 of the spread, paired t p = 0.416), and within 0.0027 of nu = 5. Represented by student_t_nu5.

not_run.name: outlier_p01
not_run.why: Within 0.0047 R2 of Gaussian at the reporting level (0.29 of the spread, paired t p = 0.178). Represented by outlier_p10.

not_run.name: outlier_p05
not_run.why: Within 0.0034 R2 of Gaussian at the reporting level (0.21 of the spread, paired t p = 0.239). Represented by outlier_p10. Note that outlier_p05 minus outlier_p01 reaches paired t p = 0.002 on LightGBM on a difference of +0.0049 R2 -- precision around zero, and the next step of the same ladder goes the other way at -0.0019, so it is not a dose response.

not_run.name: skewed_draw
not_run.why: A centred Gamma draw, asymmetric by draw rather than by mechanism. Tested in scripts/setting_selection_test.py and NOT built into either injector. Nothing at the reporting level -- 0.0016 R2, 0.10 of the spread, paired t p = 0.604. At level 1.5 it does separate on the random forest, -0.0445 R2 at 1.31 of the spread, paired t p = 0.007, but not on LightGBM (-0.0073, 0.13 of the spread, p = 0.571). One model at one level above where the paper reports. The asymmetry story is carried by censoring and by grouped_shifted, both of which are mechanisms with sources behind them rather than a chosen distribution.

settings_that_follow._comment: The CLI defaults that make the single-setting decisions operative. Both injectors are tested against these.
